title: Fate Marable, Bix and Trumbauer on the boats
summary: Marable worked a boat; Bix and Trumbauer started on them in St. Louis, and Norvo later roomed with Trumbauer in the Whiteman band, his boyhood idol.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: Yeah. Well the reason I asked you about the black musicians, is cause you know you always here about Fate Marable and all the different guys.
Well he worked on a boat --
On the River boats.
He worked --
Well I didn't realize that Bix and Frankie Trumbauer played those boats?
Oh, yes, that's where they started in St. Louis.
Oh, so that -- just as jobs.

YEAH. I later roomed with Frankie in Paul Whiteman's band -- talk about -- and I was a kid when I stood there and listened to him, he was my idol. My goodness I used to think he was the greatest thing since hash. Frankie Trumbauer. And Bix, I thought, oh, my. And, he was.
Well I mean who -- I mean would they be a part of a group --
They were a set band. They were hired on that boat. They --
Well who else was in that? Band? Can
you remember? Well drummer was Ray Ludwig, I don't remember, now. My goodness, you're talking about --
I know I am --
-- 60 years ago.
I know it -- I know it.
Nearly. I don't remember that.
It'd be like five or six -- five or six musicians?
Yeah, there'd be a trumpet, trombone or saxophone, and three rhythm. Be six --
Yeah.
-- at least, maybe seven sometimes.
How about that?
And sometimes they were bigger. Fate Marable worked -- I heard him on a boat.
Yeah.
I heard Louis on the Capitol.
Oh.

I forget the boat was, I think, that Frankie was on. Ah, don't remember. I know one of the boats was the Julie Belle Swain, which number of years later I saw down in New Orleans, but when I opened the Royal Sonesta, about six-seven years ago.
Really?

Yeah. And, fella said, 'Come down and I'll take you around the city, and I said, 'What boat?' he said, 'Julie Belle Swain,' I nearly fell down. Because later this Mel Hewlitt and the Skinner boys worked on that same boat.
Really?
Yeah. And, oh, the boats were -- the River was a beautiful thing in those days.
Yeah, I bet it was.
They hadn't cut through to the Chicago River, which made a passage from Chicago down to St. Louis, see you can go all the way, the Great Lakes, yeah, down to New Orleans.
Yeah -- well -
